    Bar snacksKensington tomato pie squaresThick Philly bakery focaccia spread with slow-cooked sweet tomato sauce, served at room temperature with pecorino and oreganoHow to make it400g bread flour7g dried yeast2 tsp caster sugar, 1 for the dough, 1 for the sauce1 tsp salt300ml warm water4 tbsp olive oil, 2 for the dough, 2 for the sauce800g tinned crushed tomatoes2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp dried oregano30g pecorino, finely gratedMix the flour, yeast, salt, a teaspoon of sugar, the water and 2 tbsp oil into a soft dough and knead for 5 minutes.Cover and leave to rise until doubled. Meanwhile simmer the tomatoes with 2 tbsp oil, the garlic, a teaspoon of oregano and the last of the sugar until thick.Oil a deep baking tray, press the dough out to the edges and leave to puff. Heat the oven to 220°C.Spread the sauce thickly over the dough right to the edges and bake until the base is crisp underneath.Cool to room temperature.Dust with the pecorino and the rest of the oregano and cut into squares.Old neighbourhood roast pork rollsMickey's gym reopens on the old block. Roast pork, broccolini and provolone in soft rollsHow to make it800g pork neck, in one piece6 garlic cloves, crushed, 4 for the pork, 2 for the greens1 tsp fennel seeds, crushed1 tbsp rosemary, chopped3 tbsp olive oil250ml chicken stock2 bunches of broccolini1/2 tsp chilli flakes8 slices of sharp provolone8 soft white rollssalt and pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 160°C. Rub the pork all over with 4 of the garlic cloves, the fennel seeds, rosemary, 1 tbsp oil and plenty of salt and pepper.Sit in a small roasting dish, pour in the stock, cover tightly with foil and roast until very tender.Rest, then slice as thinly as you can and return the slices to the juices.Fry the broccolini in the rest of the oil with the last 2 garlic cloves and the chilli flakes until tender and catching. Season.Split the rolls, pile in the pork, a slice of provolone and the broccolini, and spoon over some juices.Potato pierogi with fried onionPotato pierogi, fried onion.
